name: Tirzah
overview: Tirzah is a female member of the tribe of Manasseh, known primarily as the daughter of Zelophehad. Her mention in Scripture is brief and focused on her family identity. There are no additional notes or expanded narratives about her life in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name Tirzah means "pleasant one" or "compensation," reflecting a meaningful Hebrew designation. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God but carries a positive connotation as recorded in Numbers 26:33.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Tirzah as the daughter of Zelophehad. No other family relationships are documented in the biblical text beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Tirzah's significance in the biblical narrative lies in her identification as a daughter of Zelophehad from the tribe of Manasseh. Although the text does not elaborate on her personal story, her mention preserves the lineage and inheritance rights of Zelophehad's family within Israel. This reference underscores the importance of family lines and tribal affiliation in the Old Testament context.
